text: Before approval: Testing mode is limited to 100 test users listed on the consent screen.
quote: Projects configured with a publishing status of Testing are limited to up to 100 test users listed in the OAuth consent screen.

text: Before approval: test-user authorizations and refresh tokens expire 7 days after consent.
quote: Authorizations by a test user will expire seven days from the time of consent. If your OAuth client requests an offline access type and receives a refresh token, that token will also expire.

text: Before approval: an In-production app requesting unapproved sensitive or restricted scopes shows the unverified app screen.
quote: Google will display an Unverified apps warning message if your project's OAuth clients request authorization of scopes considered sensitive or restricted before your project has completed verification

text: Before approval: unverified apps are capped at 100 new users for the lifetime of the project, and the cap cannot be reset.
quote: unverified apps that are accessing restricted or sensitive scopes have a 100 new-user cap restriction
note: Page qualifies the cap to unverified apps accessing sensitive/restricted scopes (implied by YouTube context). Same page: 'the user cap applies over the entire lifetime of the project, and it cannot be reset or changed.'

text: Before a quota audit: default quota is 100 search.list calls, 100 videos.insert calls and 10,000 units a day for all other endpoints.
quote: default quota allocation of 100 search.list calls, 100 videos.insert calls, and 10,000 units per day combined for all other endpoints

text: Verify ownership of your authorized domains in Google Search Console.
quote: Verify ownership of your project's authorized domains within the Google Search Console .

text: Host a public home page and a privacy policy on the same domain, both linked from the consent screen.
quote: The privacy policy must be visible to users, hosted within the same domain as your application's home page, and linked to on the OAuth consent screen
note: Home page must also be publicly accessible; home page URI is part of consent screen branding.

text: The privacy policy must disclose how the app accesses, uses, stores, or shares Google user data.
quote: The privacy policy must disclose the manner in which your application accesses, uses, stores, or shares Google user data.

text: Give a written justification for each sensitive scope, including why a narrower scope is not enough.
quote: Prepare a detailed justification for each requested sensitive scope, as well as an explanation for why a narrower scope isn't sufficient.

text: Submit an unlisted YouTube video showing the consent flow, the client ID in the address bar, and each scope in use.
quote: Upload the video to YouTube Studio and set its Visibility as Unlisted .
note: Page also requires showing the consent flow, the client ID in the address bar, and functionality enabled by each sensitive scope.

text: You must publish your branding before you can request verification for data access.
quote: Note that you must have a published branding status before you can request verification for data access.

text: More quota than the default requires passing a YouTube API Services compliance audit.
quote: If you would like to request additional quota beyond the default allocation, you must first complete an audit to show that your project is in compliance with the YouTube API Services Terms of Service

text: Internal-only apps (Workspace-owned project, Internal audience) skip verification and the 100-user cap but only work in that org.
quote: Your app will not be subject to the unverified app screen or the 100-user cap if it's designated as internal-only. However, only users in the Workspace or Cloud Identity organization will be able
note: Page also says the project must be owned by the organization and the consent screen configured for internal use.

text: Google lists deleting a YouTube video as an example of a sensitive scope.
quote: Examples of sensitive scopes include reading events stored in Google Calendar, storing a new contact in Google Contacts, or deleting a YouTube video.

text: No YouTube Data API scope appears on Google's restricted scope list.
quote: The following scopes are categorized as "restricted"
note: Verified by absence: list covers Gmail, Drive, Fit, Chat, Data Portability, Photos Ambient, Health APIs; no YouTube Data API scope. Note: Data Portability API scopes like dataportability.youtube.channel are restricted.

text: Composio says its managed YouTube app's quota is shared across users and recommends your own app for production.
quote: If you use the managed/default OAuth app, that quota can be shared across users, so production workloads can hit provider quota limits faster than expected.
fix: Composio says its managed YouTube app's quota can be shared across users and recommends creating your own Google Cloud OAuth app for production.
note: Read via the page's .md version (FAQ is collapsed in HTML). Page hedges 'can be shared', claim says 'is shared'.

text: YouTube runs periodic audits and requires a form if your company changes control.
quote: We conduct periodic audits to ensure quality, improve our products and services, and verify your compliance
note: Change of control: 'must fill out and submit the Change of Control Form.'

text: Google's FAQ estimates sensitive scope verification at 10 business days, which is longer than the 3-5 days on the developer page.
quote: 10 Business days
note: FAQ table gives 10 business days (estimates not guaranteed). The 3-5 day figure is not on this page; it is on the sensitive-scope-verification developer page ('typically takes 3-5 business days'), verified there.

text: Limits apply to refresh tokens: 100 per Google Account per client ID, and creating a new one silently invalidates the oldest.
quote: There is currently a limit of 100 refresh tokens per Google Account per OAuth 2.0 client ID. If the limit is reached, creating a new refresh token automatically invalidates the oldest

text: Refresh tokens stop working after 6 months unused or if the user revokes access.
quote: The refresh token has not been used for six months.
note: Page lists these among several reasons (also password change with Gmail scopes, token limit, time-based access, admin policy); user revocation is listed too.

text: Your OAuth redirect URI must exactly match oauth_redirect_uri in the Composio auth config; some defaults still use /api/v1/auth-apps/add.
quote: The redirect URI in your OAuth app must exactly match `oauth_redirect_uri` in your Composio auth config. Some toolkit defaults still use `https://backend.composio.dev/api/v1/auth-apps/add`
note: Read via the .md version. Page is marked Legacy.

text: Use separate Google Cloud projects for testing and production, and submit only the production project for verification.
quote: Please create separate projects for development/testing/staging and production as per the Google OAuth policy .
note: Same page: 'You should only submit “production” tier projects for verification.'

text: Workspace admins can restrict sensitive scopes to OAuth clients they explicitly mark as trusted.
quote: Google Workspace organization administrators might restrict access to sensitive scopes to prevent access by OAuth client IDs that the organization doesn't explicitly mark as trusted.

text: Google OAuth sensitive scope verification; a YouTube compliance audit only to raise quota | wait: 3-5 business days for OAuth (audit wait not stated)
quote: The sensitive scope verification process typically takes 3-5 business days to complete.
note: The YouTube compliance audit part is not on this page; it is supported by the quota_and_compliance_audits page, which gives no audit wait time.

text: Before approval: you only have development keys; the production Show Credentials switch stays hidden.
quote: Note: The Show Credentials switch appears only after the App Assessment Questionnaire is approved.
note: Rendered with Playwright. 'Only development keys' is not stated outright but follows from production credentials being hidden.

text: Builder tier: 500,000 CorePlus API calls per month, and calls above that are blocked.
quote: the Builder tier will be limited to 500,000 CorePlus API credits per month. Any CorePlus API calls made above the included monthly credit will be blocked entirely.
note: Rendered with Playwright.

text: Production app details need EULA and privacy policy URLs, host domain, launch, disconnect and connect/reconnect URLs.
quote: enter the URLs for your End User License Agreement and Privacy Policy. In the next, add your app's host domain, launch URL, disconnect URL, and connect/reconnect URL.

text: Production redirect URIs must use https, and IP addresses are not allowed.
quote: The Intuit OAuth 2.0 Server can only redirect to URIs beginning with https. IP addresses aren't allowed.
note: Stated under the production apps section.

text: You must get the App Assessment Questionnaire approved to see production credentials.
quote: Note: The Show Credentials switch appears only after the App Assessment Questionnaire is approved.

text: Listed apps must be on the Silver tier or above to avoid delisting.
quote: your app listing will temporarily remain in place, but is subject to removal from the Intuit App Marketplace. To avoid a delisting, you must subscribe to Silver.

text: Access tokens last 1 hour; refresh tokens expire after 100 days unused.
quote: Access tokens are valid for 3,600 seconds (or one hour).
note: Also: 'If the refresh token hasn't been used in the last 100 days ... the refresh token expires.'

text: The refresh token value rotates every 24 hours, so always store the latest one.
quote: We update the value of the refresh_token value every 24 hours hours, or the next time you refresh the access tokens after 24 hours.
note: Page recommends always storing the latest refresh_token value.

text: Refresh tokens have a hard limit of 5 years, after which users must reconnect.
quote: Refresh tokens have a hard limit of 5 years. After that, your app must ask users to reauthorize the connection.

text: Development and production keys are separate, and sandbox redirect URIs can use localhost.
quote: Each app has two URIs: one for testing environments (i.e., sandboxes), and another for live, in-production apps.
fix: Sandbox and production redirect URIs are set separately, and sandbox redirect URIs can use localhost without HTTPS.
note: Page confirms localhost for sandbox ('You can add localhost (no HTTPS) as a URI for sandbox environments') but is about redirect URIs; it does not say development and production keys are separate.

text: The com.intuit.quickbooks.payment scope can cause Cloudflare Error 1016 if Payments is not enabled.
quote: If this appears while connecting QuickBooks and the auth config includes the `com.intuit.quickbooks.payment` scope, check whether the QuickBooks Payments module is enabled
note: Read via the .md version.

text: Sandbox connections need https://sandbox-quickbooks.api.intuit.com as the base URL in Composio.
quote: For QuickBooks sandbox accounts, pass `https://sandbox-quickbooks.api.intuit.com` as the URL/base URL when initiating the connection.

text: The Intuit App Partner Program is available only to partners in the US, UK, Australia and Canada (excluding Quebec).
quote: The Intuit App Partner Program is available for partners based in the US, UK, Australia, and Canada (excluding Quebec).
note: Stated in the page footer.

text: Intuit App Assessment Questionnaire, approved before production keys are shown | wait: not stated
quote: Note: The Show Credentials switch appears only after the App Assessment Questionnaire is approved.
note: No review wait time is stated; page says Step 1 app details take about 30 minutes.

text: $0 on the Builder tier; Silver is $300 USD/month
quote: The first monthly Program Fee is charged for $300 USD
note: Builder tier is uncharged. $300 is from the US Silver example; UK is £225 and Canada $425. Variable CorePlus API fees apply above Silver's included 1,000,000 calls.

text: Pay-per-use plans are capped at 3 million Post reads per monthly billing cycle.
quote: Pay-per-usage plans are capped at **3 million Post reads per monthly billing cycle**.
note: Fetched raw Markdown from GitHub.

text: API requests are blocked when your credit balance or spending limit runs out.
quote: When the limit is reached, API requests will be blocked until the next billing cycle.
note: Also: if the credit balance goes negative, 'API requests will be blocked until you add credits'.

text: Posts with a URL cost $0.20 per request.
quote: | **Post: Create (with URL)** | $0.200 per request |

text: You must sign in at console.x.com, accept the Developer Agreement and Policy, and describe your use.
quote: Review and accept the Developer Agreement and Policy.
note: Step 3: 'Provide basic information about how you'll use the API.'

text: Callback URLs must be allowlisted, match exactly, and use https in production.
quote:
- Add callback URLs to your app's allowlist in the Developer Console
- URLs must match exactly (including trailing slashes)
note: Also: 'Use https:// in production'.

text: Choose Web App or Automated App to get a client secret (confidential client).
quote: **Confidential clients** receive a Client Secret. **Public clients** use PKCE only.
note: Web App and Automated App / Bot are listed as Confidential.

text: Access tokens last two hours, and refresh tokens are only issued with the offline.access scope.
quote: By default, the access token you create through the Authorization Code Flow with PKCE will only stay valid for two hours unless you’ve used the `offline.access` scope.
fix: By default, access tokens are valid for two hours unless the offline.access scope is used, and refresh tokens are only issued with the offline.access scope.
note: Refresh-token half confirmed ('If this scope is not passed, we will not generate a refresh token'). Claim drops the page's 'by default ... unless offline.access' qualifier on the two-hour lifetime.

text: Credentials are shown once; losing them means regenerating and invalidating the old ones.
quote: Credentials are only displayed once. Store them in a password manager or secure vault. If you lose them, you'll need to regenerate (which invalidates the old ones).

text: Composio managed credentials for Twitter were removed in February 2026.
quote: As of February 2026, Composio managed credentials for the Twitter toolkit have been removed.
note: Read via the .md version.

text: Post analytics actions return 403 unless you are on an X Enterprise plan.
quote: Requires an X Enterprise API plan. Accounts on Free, Basic, Pro, or Pay-Per-Use tiers will receive a 403 Forbidden on every call
note: From the TWITTER_GET_POST_ANALYTICS tool description.

text: Apps can have at most 10 callback URLs.
quote: Maximum of **10 callback URLs** per app

text: First-time credit incentives ($20 plus up to $50 match) expire 3 months after they are granted.
quote: Free credits from these incentives **expire 3 months after they are granted**.
note: $20 requires completing a first credit purchase (adding a card alone no longer qualifies since Oct 13, 2026).

text: Pay-per-use credits, e.g. $0.005 per post read and $0.015 per post created
quote: | **Posts: Read** | $0.005 per resource |
note: Post: Create is $0.015 per request. Owned Reads are $0.001.

text: Connect OAuth with read_write cannot connect to Standard accounts controlled by another platform.
quote: Platforms using OAuth with `read_write` scope can’t connect to Standard accounts that are controlled by another platform.
note: Fetched via the page's .md version.

text: Stripe Apps before publishing: external testing is capped at 25 testers per app.
quote: There is a limit of 25 testers per app.

text: Each redirect URI must be listed in Connect OAuth settings, and live mode redirect URIs must use HTTPS.
quote: To protect yourself from certain forms of man-in-the-middle attacks, the live mode `redirect_uri` must use a secure HTTPS connection.
note: Also: 'In your platform settings, add each redirect URI.'

text: Stripe Apps review needs test credentials, testing guidance and the live-mode public install URL.
quote: When submitting your application for review, you must use Live mode Public Install URL.
note: Public Install URL requirement is stated for OAuth apps. Testing guidance and test credentials are both listed review fields.

text: Your business cannot be on Stripe's prohibited and restricted businesses list to publish an app.
quote: Your business purpose can’t be on the Stripe [Prohibited and Restricted Businesses](https://stripe.com/legal/restricted-businesses) list.

text: Stripe says OAuth is not recommended for new Connect platforms.
quote: OAuth isn’t recommended for new
note: Stripe recommends Connect Onboarding for Standard accounts instead. Full sentence: 'OAuth isn’t recommended for new Connect platforms.'

text: New Connect extensions can no longer be built; Stripe Apps replaced them.
quote: You can no longer build new Connect extensions.
note: Page heading: 'Stripe Apps replaces Connect extensions'.

text: Only extensions can use the read_only scope, so new platforms get read_write.
quote: Only Extensions can use `read_only`, which ensures that platforms can’t read other applications’ data.
note: 'So new platforms get read_write' is an inference; the OAuth reference says scope defaults to read_only, which only extensions can use, so platforms must pass read_write.

text: The Connect token call uses your platform's secret API key as client_secret.
quote: Make this call using your secret API key as a `client_secret` POST parameter:

text: Each client_id is either live or test, so use the matching one per environment.
quote: Each `client_id` is either a live or test ID. Use a Sandbox `client_id` to connect to a Sandbox account.

text: Stripe Apps OAuth access tokens expire in 1 hour; refresh tokens last 1 year and roll on use.
quote: Access tokens expire in 1 hour, and refresh tokens expire after 1 year. Refresh tokens are also rolled on every exchange
